$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-09-07 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 2cd05892. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v35 index for sub2api (INDEX 95f6319c) built by publish-tee-images run 34079063403 from commit 6e2d439e0; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin (INDEX cef1d03d) because deploy/attestor carries no functional change (only a .dockerignore edit), and repinning it would widen the attested surface for nothing. VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated plainly: composeHash, osImageHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones. The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - the workflow performs the signing and its run succeeded, and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below, but this file does not claim it was done. This release is a large upstream sync: the fork was merged up to upstream version 0.2.1, bringing 89 upstream commits including support for a newer OpenAI model family (GPT-6 Astra) and other provider improvements, on top of the fork's own two-sided-market work. Of the files changed on both sides only twelve overlapped; the notable reconciliations were the client-version pin and floor (kept, baseline at the level required by the newer Claude models, now composing with upstream's environment-overridable version mechanism), the scheduling gate (the fork's own combined window-cost/RPM/daily-cap gate was kept over upstream's parallel window-cost/RPM gates since they implement the same function and the fork's is what production runs, while upstream's channel-restriction gate was adopted), and the ORM generated code (regenerated from the merged schema). It DOES add schema migrations from upstream; those coexist with the fork's own migrations because the migration runner keys applied migrations by filename, not by numeric prefix, so same-numbered files from both lineages apply independently - production already contained several such same-numbered pairs. The whole merge was verified before rollout: full backend build and vet, the entire backend test suite, frontend type-check build and unit tests, and a full-startup rehearsal against a restored copy of the production database in which every migration applied in interleaved order and the application initialized and served health with no panic. A full postgres backup was taken and verified immediately beforehand - downloaded from S3, gzip-tested, 110 COPY sections - and it is the rollback point for the schema change. Earlier in this line: proof-v34 (fingerprint version floor so accounts stuck on an old impersonated client version are raised on read), proof-v33 (raise the built-in impersonated client version to the newer Claude models' minimum), proof-v32 (two distinct experiences for consumer and contributor over one shared account, plus an attach-time model-quota probe), proof-v31 (recompute one internal account's historical earnings, a data migration), proof-v30 (skipped), v29, v28, v27, v26 (earlier upstream sync, Claude Fable 5.1), v24, v23..v15. osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation, and the control plane confirms is_dev false after the rollout. This rollout completed in 100 seconds with no incident.
